topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I can scarce believe it, William telling me that young Edmund's come back, but he don't recall his own childhood. It's like the earth swallowing up memories, leaving naught but silence. I remember when the two of them would run by our fields, yelling and laughing, almost scaring the crows away. How could Edmund not recall that? Or the time we spent catching frogs by the old mill stream? I've been thinking on it, how I should’ve reached out to him sooner, maybe talked about the old days, could’ve jogged his memory. But I lingered, hesitating, and now I wonder what’s become of our friendship, if there’s anything left at all. The soil holds its secrets, but I fear this one may never give up its rest.
